text:
jamie: quick sync — I'm drafting a PRD for a metrics UX focused on SLO-aligned dashboards for the Console. Goal: make it trivial for customers to map Redwood latency/cost SLOs to dashboard views and alerts. draft: https://docs.google.com/draft-metrics-ux (WIP)

maria: looked at the draft, big 👍 on the SLO->widget mapping. can we be explicit about the data cardinality we expect? large tenants will have 100s of routes.

sahil: agree on cardinality. we also need guardrails for query cost & time ranges — don't let dashboard presets create 1h*100routes queries by default. maybe cap auto-queries or use async thumbnails.

monica: from DX side, customers keep asking for a one-click 'Investigate' flow that opens traces for the selected query window. we should include a small flow chart in the PRD.

rick: UX note — prioritise a single top-level SLO selector. users pick an SLO (e.g., p95 latency 200ms) and the UI should surface related traces, slowest routes, cohort comparisons. see quick mock: /images/mock-slo-selector.png (placeholder)

jamie: thanks. proposed scope (MVP):
1) SLO selector + prebuilt SLO widgets (latency p50/p95, tail error rate, cost/tokens)
2) Per-route breakdown table with sort & pagination (supports >200 routes)
3) One-click Investigate -> opens trace view filtered by route/time window
4) Retention/aggregation tiers toggle (1m raw for 7d, 5m for 30d, 1h for 365d)
5) Launch criteria + rollout plan

maria: engineering constraints to call out for PRD:
- backend: aggregated metrics store read path needs parameterized rollup levels (1m/5m/1h)
- storage: ensure we can backfill if customer upgrades retention tiers
- perf: queries for default dashboard must return <1s for up to 200 routes

sahil: SRE concerns / acceptance criteria:
- no dashboard query should exceed 5x baseline QPS per org during rollout
- auto-fallback to cached snapshot on query timeouts
- canary: enable for 10 customers, synthetic load test ramp to 5x

jamie: initial acceptance criteria (MVP) — please validate/edit: 
- AC1: Users can select an SLO and see matching widgets within 1s median response
- AC2: Per-route table supports sort/paginate across 500 routes with median response <2s
- AC3: One-click Investigate launches trace view filtered correctly and loads within 2s for canary tenants
- AC4: Retention tiers documented and applied; backfill runs without blocking UI
- AC5: Rollout plan exists with canary gating metrics and rollback steps

monica: add AC for discoverability: onboarding tooltip + quick tour must be present for first-time users.

rick: add AC for mobile/responsive table collapse behavior.

maria: implementation edge cases to add to PRD:
- routing policies: queries should respect customer region data locality (EU customers hitting EU storage)
- model of missing data: show 'data gaps' badges when rollups are incomplete (explain in tooltip)
- mixed-tenancy: when Dedicated customers have private retention, ensure UI hides unsupported retention toggles

jamie: excellent. two product tradeoffs to call out in PRD:
- Aggressive pre-aggregation reduces compute cost but increases storage and adds lag to newest data. recommend 1m raw for 7d then 5m/1h rollups.
- Enabling per-route default dashboard for orgs with >500 routes could be expensive; propose opt-in via 'enable route table' toggle in org settings.

sahil: operational notes for rollout section:
- metrics: p95 dashboard render latency, backend query error rate, cache hit rate, storage backfill lag
- run synthetic traffic during canary at realistic route fanout patterns (skewed distribution)
- require automatic throttle if dashboard QPS exceeds safety threshold

jamie: customers who've asked: Acme Labs (needs SLO-driven traces), FinServ Co (retention compliance), NoticeHealth (route cardinality). Will include their asks as acceptance examples in PRD.

monica: docs + quickstarts to ship with launch: 1) How to create SLO-backed dashboards 2) Troubleshooting guide for data gaps 3) Best practices for low-cost dashboards.

maria: timeline re: infra work — estimate 3 wks infra to add rollups + backfill job, 2 wks to expose APIs, 3 wks frontend integration. so 8–9wks end-to-end assuming no surprises.

jamie: proposed rollout plan (high-level):
- Week 0: RFC signoff & infra spike
- Week 3: backend rollup & API ready (internal demo)
- Week 6: frontend MVP behind feature flag + internal QA
- Week 8: canary with 10 customers, run 2-week validation window
- Week 10: gradual rollout + docs

sahil: +1, add automatic rollback on error-rate > 2% sustained for 10m during canary.

rick: small UX follow-ups: expose 'compare cohorts' in MVP as hidden opt-in feature flag so we can iterate quickly.

jamie: action items:
- jamie: update PRD with ACs, rollout plan, and customer examples (by EOD Thu)
- maria: produce infra design doc + backfill sketch (by Mon)
- monica: draft onboarding copy + quickstart (by Mon)
- rick: produce small mocks for SLO selector and Investigate flow (by Thu)
- sahil: define canary gating metrics & synthetic load plan (by Mon)

deploy-bot: Created: deployment-checklist/metrics-ux-prd (ticket #4281)

maria: noted on ticket, will link infra doc when ready.

jamie: thanks all. if no objections I'll mark RFC ready for review tomorrow and ping eng-platform + eng-sre reviewers.

sahil: no objections from me. :thumbsup:

monica: no objections. small nit: add an accessibility check in ACs.

jamie: added accessibility AC: dashboard controls keyboard-focusable and aria labels for SLO selector.

rick: LGTM

jamie: closing thread — will post updated PRD link after edits. :wave:
